title: Terraform VPC Network Module: zonal subnet tiers, managed egress adapters, interface endpoints, and proactive route-health probes
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Private deployments require a single, opinionated Terraform VPC module that provides predictable, observable egress behavior across zones, simplifies customer configuration, and proactively detects routing/egress failures. Current infra pieces are fragmented across multiple modules and ad-hoc scripts which causes drift during upgrades and makes post-deploy incidents noisy for SREs and customers.

Goal: Build a composable Terraform module that provisions zonal subnet tiers (control/data/aux), attaches managed egress adapters (NAT Gateway or managed NAT instances or IGW depending on customer preference), registers recommended interface and gateway VPC endpoints, and wires in lightweight route/endpoint health probes with SNS/CloudWatch alerts so operators can detect egress path regressions before customer traffic is affected. The module must be parametric for AZ counts and support a toggle between “managed” egress (Redwood-managed NAT autoscaling instances) and cloud-native NAT Gateway for cost/latency trade-offs.

Scope: Module resources (subnets, route tables, NAT/IGW, egress adapter autoscaling group IAM policies), endpoint mappings (s3, sts, ecr, secretsmanager, kms via interface endpoints), route table generation per subnet tier, and a small Lambda probe + CloudWatch metric+alarm that verifies route reachability to a set of canonical endpoints. Also provide Terraform upgrade guide and automated upgrade plan checks (terraform plan diff validation) to reduce upgrade-time regressions.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Managed egress adapters (autoscaling NAT instances) reduce per-byte cost and allow more deterministic routing/observability hooks (tcp dumps/metrics), but increase operational surface area and require hardened AMIs + image rotation.
- NAT Gateway offers lower ops cost and SLA but higher per-byte cost and less visibility. Expose this as a top-level toggle with recommended defaults per customer tier.
- Route health probes will use a minimal Lambda (Node 18) that tests connectivity to a set of endpoints through each route table; probe failures will synthesize a per-route CloudWatch metric and create SNS notifications. Probes must run at low frequency (5m) to avoid noise but fast enough for early detection.
- Endpoint policy attachments should default to least-privilege for customer-managed services; we provide optional templates to allow privileged diagnostic endpoints for SREs.

Acceptance criteria: - Module can be instantiated in a 3-AZ account with default settings and create: 3 zonal subnet tiers, route tables, either managed egress adapters or NAT Gateways, and required VPC endpoints. - Route-health probe Lambda executes successfully and produces CloudWatch metrics for each route table. - Module outputs include: subnet ids by tier, route table ids by tier, chosen egress mode, endpoints created, and probe dashboard URL. - Terraform plan drift check: a pipeline job runs terraform plan and fails on any diff that changes route table or egress configurations without an explicit override flag. - Upgrade guide and a migration script for customers moving from NAT Gateway to managed egress and back.

Deliverables: Terraform module under infra/modules/vpc-networking, example root module for customer/private deployment, a CI job that runs terraform fmt/validate/plan, Lambda probe code + Terraform that deploys it, CloudWatch dashboard template, and a Confluence runbook describing upgrade steps and known limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Instantiate module in a 3-AZ test account with default settings: create subnet tiers, route tables, egress resources, and endpoints
Route-health probe Lambda runs and emits CloudWatch metrics for each route table within 5 minutes of deployment
Outputs include subnet ids by tier, route table ids, egress mode, endpoints created, and probe dashboard URL
CI pipeline enforces terraform plan drift checks: any change to route/egress requires explicit approval flag
Provide an upgrade guide and migration helpers for switching egress modes without traffic disruption
comments: 2025-02-11 — Asha Menon: Initial PRD posted to Confluence (link below). Started spike to compare NAT Gateway vs managed NAT instance TCO across sample traffic profiles.

2025-02-13 — Luca Romero: Spike results show managed NAT instances reduce bytes cost by ~40% at high egress volumes but add 1-2 hours of operational runbook steps during AMI rotation. Propose default: NAT Gateway for <2TB/month customers, managed egress for >=2TB with opt-in.

2025-02-15 — Eng architectural review: Decided to implement probes as single Lambda per VPC that iterates route tables to reduce Lambda cold-start footprint. Action: add IAM policy scope to allow probe to run DescribeRouteTables and perform minimal TCP checks via VPC ENI.

2025-02-17 — Security review notes: AMI hardening and image rotation required for managed adapters. Assigned to EngSec for AMI baseline. Also require KMS CMK usage for endpoint policy secrets. Security review kickoff scheduled.
2025-02-18 — PR feedback (infra repo): Split module into core (subnets/routes) and extras (egress, probes, endpoints) so customers can opt-in. Luca to draft module composition PRs.
2025-02-19 — QA notes: Need test harness to simulate AZ blackhole by modifying route to a dead ENI; will add a small terratest suite to CI that toggles a test route and verifies probe alarms trigger.
2025-02-20 — Product review: PM approved scope for initial rollout to beta customers. Action: schedule private beta with two customers in Cycle 43 and prepare migration guide.
notes: Keep API of module small: input map for subnet-count-by-az and egress_mode enum (nat_gateway | managed_nat | igw)
Provide example var files for small/medium/enterprise customer profiles
Make probe optional via variable enable_route_probes = true|false to avoid extra AWS charges in experimental accounts
